Jawai first played for the [[Cairns Marlins]] in the [[Queensland Basketball League]] in 2004, before heading to Canberra the following year to attend the [[Australian Institute of Sport]]. He went on to play for the [[Cairns Taipans]] in the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] before being drafted by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. Two years later he joined [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] in Serbia, then Barcelona and Turkey, before heading back home to Australia and winning an [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] with the [[Perth Wildcats]] in 2016. Standing at 209 cm, he played at the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|centre]] positions. Jawai played for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 FIBA World Cup]]. ==Early life== Jawai was born in [[Sydney]], New South Wales, in the suburb of [[Paddington, New South Wales|Paddington]], on 10 October 1986,{{cite web |title=Nate Jawai |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/53615/sid/8054/tid/239/tid2//_/2015_FIBA_Oceania_Championship/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=1 December 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151118031026/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/53615/sid/8054/tid/239/tid2//_/2015_FIBA_Oceania_Championship/index.html |archive-date=18 November 2015}} to parents Ron and Lynette.{{cite news|url=https://www.athletesvoice.com.au/nate-jawai-cape-york-nba-back/|title=Cape York to the NBA & back|work=[[Athletes Voice]]|author=Jawai, Nate |date=23 September 2018|accessdate=12 November 2021}} He grew up in [[Bamaga]], 40 km from the tip of [[Cape York Peninsula]].{{cite news |last1=Nagy |first1=Boti |title=Perth Wildcats superstar Nathan Jawai out to beast Adelaide 36ers when NBL season gets under way |url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/basketball/perth-wildcats-superstar-nathan-jawai-out-to-beast-adelaide-36ers-when-nbl-season-gets-under-way/news-story/6dc695b4d7feea3427d54c9f474fbee9 |access-date=1 December 2025 |work=heraldsun.com.au |date=5 October 2015}} In Bamaga, a small town of about 1000 people, his father was the local police sergeant. He is an [[Indigenous Australian]] of [[Torres Strait Islander]] descent.{{cite news|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/archive/news/indigenous-basketballer-shoots-for-top/story-e6frg6oo-1111116353848|title=Indigenous basketballer Nathan Jawai shoots for top|work=[[The Australian]]|author=Murphy, Padraic|date=16 May 2008|accessdate=27 April 2015}} Like most children on Cape York, he played [[rugby league]] throughout primary school and early high school.[http://www.theaustralian.com.au/archive/news/indigenous-basketballer-shoots-for-top/story-e6frg6oo-1111116353848 Indigenous basketballer Nathan Jawai shoots for top] However, living in a remote indigenous community meant Jawai was subject to a lot of bad influences and was often getting in trouble due to the stain of drug and alcohol abuse.[https://thewest.com.au/news/australia/wildcats-wild-ride-to-the-top-ng-ya-130444 Wildcats' wild ride to the top][https://hoopshype.com/2008/02/29/nathan-jawai-i-want-to-be-in-the-nba-next-season/ Nathan Jawai: "I want to be in the NBA next season"] Strong parental guidance and the decision to send Jawai to high school at [[St Augustine's College (Queensland)|St Augustine's College]] in [[Cairns]] ensured he stayed away from bad influences. At the age of 15, Jawai began playing basketball, and it only took him two years until he began playing competitively for the [[Cairns Marlins]] of the [[Queensland Basketball League]] in 2004.[http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/jawais-historic-raptors-contract/story-e6freyj0-1111116888951 Jawai's historic Raptors contract] {{dead link|date=December 2018}} He then spent 2005 and 2006 at the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in [[Canberra]] playing for the [[BA Centre of Excellence|AIS men's team]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL){{cite news|title=Past Athletes|work=ausport.gov.au|url=http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140212073754/http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes|archive-date=12 February 2014|url-status=dead}} before venturing to the United States to play college basketball for [[Midland College]] in 2006–07. However, after just one season with Midland, Jawai returned to Australia and had surgery to remove the meniscus in his right knee.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&aid=5037 |title=Jawai return imminent |work=NBL.com.au |date=24 May 2007 |access-date=17 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070913022239/http://www.nbl.com.au/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&aid=5037 |archive-date=13 September 2007 }} With his move back home, he had hopes of joining an [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] club.[http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/the-next-shaq-is-a-taipan/story-e6frexni-1111114739773 The next Shaq is a Taipan] He subsequently re-joined the Cairns Marlins and helped guide them to a [[List of ABA National Champions|national title]] in [[2007 Australian Club Championships|2007]] while earning [[2007 Australian Club Championships#All-Star Five|ACC All-Star Five]] honours.{{cite web | url=http://misc.sportingpulse.com/ba_annualreport/PDF/Australian%20Club%20Championships%20Scoreboard.pdf | title=Basketball career== ===Cairns Taipans=== Jawai joined the [[Cairns Taipans]] for the [[2007–08 NBL season]].{{cite news |last1=Greenwood |first1=Emma |title=Jawai joins Taipans |url=http://www.basketballwa.asn.au/fs_newsitem.asp?id=68768&orgID=1&Oname=BA&O1c=8&O10c=3 |access-date=6 November 2025 |work=basketballwa.asn.au |publisher=The Cairns Post |date=14 January 2007 games for the Taipans, Jawai averaged 17.3 points, 9.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. His season highs for points and rebounds was 28 and 18 respectively.{{cite news|title=Player statistics for Nathan Jawai|url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=190394815&client=0-189-88243-125701-11144829|access-date=5 December 2014|work=FoxSportsPulse.com}} ===NBA=== Jawai was drafted 41st overall in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]]; however, his rights were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in a deal that also brought [[Jermaine O'Neal]] to Toronto in exchange for [[T. J. Ford]], [[Rasho Nesterović]], [[Maceo Baston]], and the draft rights to [[Roy Hibbert]].{{cite news|title=Australian league rookie of year Jawai signs with Raptors|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3483725|access-date=5 December 2014|work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|date=11 July 2008}}{{cite news|title=Pacers, Raptors complete trade sending O'Neal to Toronto|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3480419|access-date=5 December 2014|work=ESPN.com|date=9 July 2008}} On 11 July 2008, he signed a two-year deal with the Raptors, and the nicknames soon rolled in with "Aussie Shaq", "Outback Shaq" and "Baby Shaq", due to his resemblance to [[Shaquille O'Neal]].{{cite news|last1=Hand |first1=Guy |title=Aussie basketball has a new star |url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/aussie-basketball-has-a-new-star/story-e6frf33c-1111115108101 |access-date=5 December 2014 |work=Foxsports.com.au |date=14 December 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810213532/http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/aussie-basketball-has-a-new-star/story-e6frf33c-1111115108101 |archive-date=10 August 2011 }}{{cite news|last1=Ulmer|first1=Mike|title=Talking With Nathan Jawai|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/jawai_073108.html|access-date=5 December 2014|work=NBA.com|date=31 July 2008}} He was also nicknamed "Big Nate" by Toronto commentators.{{cite news|title=Nathan Jawai vs Kings - All 1:49 of it !|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NC8UPK4JZwA |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/NC8UPK4JZwA |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=5 December 2014|work=Youtube.com|date=25 January 2009}}{{cbignore}} On 17 December 2008, Jawai was cleared to resume training after enduring a worrisome period in which he was not allowed to undergo physical activity. Jawai was required to 'rest', due to a routine pre-season test which revealed a cardiac abnormality.{{cite news|title=Jawai gets all-clear to resume his career|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/sport/jawai-gets-allclear-to-resume-his-career/2008/12/18/1229189810268.html|access-date=5 December 2014|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=19 December 2008}} On 21 January 2009, Jawai made his NBA debut against the [[Detroit Pistons]] at [[The Palace of Auburn Hills]],{{cite news|title=Toronto Raptors vs. Detroit Pistons - Play By Play|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playbyplay?gameId=290121008|access-date=5 December 2014|work=ESPN.com|date=21 January 2009}} becoming the first indigenous Australian to play in the NBA.{{Cite web
